_comment: Replay-Tickets.ps1's rubric: real past tickets the resolver is replayed against (read-only) to score a prompt/model/pipeline change before it goes live. Per ticket: ticket_id; tier (what the classifier assigned, or should have); as_of (optional Halo-time timestamp - actions after it are ignored so the ticket is judged as it stood then, and the run's clock/business-hours flag are set to it; leave out to use the first client message); must_mention / must_not_mention (regex lists, case-insensitive, checked against the resolver's whole WOULD-DO output - any miss/hit is a FAIL; write must_not patterns so a negated mention like 'no malware indicators' doesn't trip them); reply_must_mention / reply_must_not_mention (same, but checked ONLY against the client-facing reply - the text from 'Hi <name>,' to the 'Here to help' sign-off - so an internal note saying the right thing can't cover for a vague reply; a rubric with these fails if no reply segment exists); should_mention (regex list - a miss is only a WARN); expected_marker (optional list - a replay that ends on HUMAN_OWNED or BLOCKED never investigated and is a FAIL unless that marker is listed here); keep_own_actions (optional, true keeps this pipeline's own notes dated at or before as_of in play instead of hiding them - for replaying a draft-revision / FLOW B scenario, which only works while the draft note still exists in Halo: FLOW B deletes superseded drafts and FLOW A collapses approved ones, so a past ticket's draft state is usually gone); notes (for humans). Replays run in the same approval mode as the registered scheduled task unless -RequireApproval is given explicitly. This file is seeded once by Update-HaloResponseAgent.ps1 and never overwritten - it is this deployment's own to grow. Add a ticket here every time a real one teaches the pipeline something, so the lesson is re-checked on every future change instead of trusted to hold.

tickets.notes: Can't access S: drive. Ticket body already carried the device's IP (192.168.188.3) - Ever Frame Steel's Meraki VLAN 200 'Security', no uplink. The right answer finds that from existing tools instead of asking the client for the error message and server path (v2.10.69).

Jill Barron: 'is my laptop still under warranty?' Never send the client to look it up herself (v2.10.56/57). The warranty was never in Ninja's custom fields for this device (only mgmtLevel=Full) - NinjaOne only returns it with expand=warranty on the device GET, which ninjarmm-mcp's get_device didn't send until 2026-09-19. Device 3284's warranty ran 2020-07-20 to 2023-07-19 (get_device -> warranty_summary), so the right reply says it expired in July 2023 and moves on to the loose charging port.

Thomas Wilder (Thompson Sales) - 'computer keeps turning itself off', needs a physical power button press to come back. First-pass replay: no remote fix exists, the honest outcome is a held draft that says so and asks what the tech needs to visit. This ticket's other lesson (v2.10.61: the ticket was relinked to a contact whose Halo record carries a guessed company address, and a real reply went to twilder@thompsonsales.com instead of the gmail he writes from) can NOT be replayed here: it only exists after the relink, by which point the pipeline's own draft-revision state was later deleted by FLOW B (Halo's action list skips ids 8/10/12), and a first-pass replay after a human relink is HUMAN_OWNED by rule. The general check - compare get_contact's emailaddress with the ticket's emailtolist before any client-facing reply - is scored on every first-pass ticket via should_mention get_contact.
Stacy asks whether a Windows Update reboot prompt on Wayne's PC is legitimate. Plain answer: yes, safe to restart.

Gold Mechanical wants 20 Adobe licenses billed to AP. A complete first pass asks the CLIENT which edition (Standard vs Pro) with a brief comparison. Run history: baseline (09-19) internal note said 'Standard vs. Professional' while the client got a vague 'looping in our team' holding reply; baseline2 same; baseline3 asked the question properly in the draft (17 turns). Same prompt each time - this ticket flips on its own, so a single-run change here is noise; re-run it before believing a delta.
reply_must_not_mention: looping in our team|we'?ll follow up shortly with next steps

tickets.notes: Travis asks for Google Chrome. Policy: recommend Edge first with one brief reason, never refuse Chrome (v2.10.67).

Leaver/offboarding request with multiple account removals and mailbox redirects - outside the whitelist, needs a human via M365 admin; the right outcome is a held draft plus escalation, never an attempted remediation.
JumpCloud account locked after repeated login failures; JumpCloud already sent reactivation instructions; the contact doesn't exist in Halo yet.

BEC CFO: Hannah Merano can't access Outlook. Same client and same account as #22296's JumpCloud lockout minutes earlier - a real diagnosis checks the account's actual state (CIPP/M365 and JumpCloud) and connects the two, rather than asking the client what error she sees. This is also the ticket a resolver pass abandoned without a single tool call (v2.10.68) - a replay that ends with no facts found is a FAIL by rubric.
Closed by Erick with a real fix (Bluebeam update, plotter driver install, calendar fix). LEARN_FIX should read what he did and decide whether it's worth documenting - not re-solve it.

Springfield Nissan 3CX down (multiple users can't sign in) on a Saturday morning. Charles emailed admin@altecsales.com; Michael forwarded it into help@ hours later, so the ticket's first message opens with Michael's signature and a quoted From/To header. Two things to score: it reads as an outage (emergency acknowledgment + on-call), and - v2.12.3 - the first reply includes one warm line asking Charles to write to help@altecusa.com or call next time because an individual inbox creates no ticket and isn't monitored. Also arrived linked to the generic Unknown client: the right pass relinks to Springfield Nissan.
reply_must_mention: not (actively )?monitored|doesn'?t create a ticket|don'?t create a ticket
reply_must_not_mention: should have|you must|please do not|in future you
